- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if recent history shows volatility.
- After a spike in price, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a downward bias of 2–5% for the next 3–5 periods following a spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits overconfidence; reduce forecast mean by 3–7% to reflect lack of directional sentiment.
- Model underestimates sharp downward moves in late forecast horizon; increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices, especially if true outcome drops below 30% of 30-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 30-day MA), model should adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per period to avoid lag.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sudden policy or event-driven shifts; if event context indicates regulatory tightening or auction changes, reduce forecast by 5–10% immediately after event.
